forward.prompt:
These are every image in one clothing SKU. Each VIEW contains an original photograph and a sheet of its SAM3 mask regions. Every mask has a UNIQUE ID beginning with R; IDs never repeat in another view.
Find every visually distinct garment that has visible pixels in an available mask in EVERY VIEW. The same garment may be shown alone, worn, from behind, as a fabric detail, or partly hidden under another layer. Use ALL views to establish identity. Do not require a small visible collar or undershirt strip to have the full garment silhouette. Match by fabric, construction, color and the context. A jacket and its undershirt remain separate garments even if the layers are sewn together. Similar colors alone are insufficient. A mask mixing different garments is not usable. Do not invent unseen pixels or new mask boundaries.
First describe which garments are present and which disappear, using the region IDs printed on the crops. Then output JSON: {"tracks":[{"garment":"description","regions":["R001", "R004", ...]}]}. This is only an output schema, not an answer. List only supplied region IDs and assign each ID to at most one track. A track must cover EVERY VIEW with at least one visible region. Extra fragments of the SAME garment in a view may share a track. Unlisted regions are removed. Keep repeated styling too, if present in every view. Do not select by the item for sale. If nothing is visibly supported everywhere, return an empty tracks list.
forward.raw:
After analyzing all views and their corresponding mask regions, we must identify garments that are **visibly present in at least one mask region in every view** (i.e., in VIEW 36601262_00 through _04). The key is to track the same garment across all views by fabric, construction, color, and context — even if it appears partially, from different angles, or under layers.

---

### Step-by-step Analysis:

#### VIEW 36601262_00:
- **R001**: Shows the front right side of a white denim jacket with black leather patch on shoulder, silver buttons, and a pocket with a label.
- **R002**: A close-up of the label in the pocket — this is a **detail**, not a garment.

→ **R001** is part of a white/black denim jacket.

#### VIEW 36601262_01:
- **R003**: Black fabric — likely the black leather panel on the left side of the jacket.
- **R004**: Side view of the jacket — white body, black leather on left side and sleeve, grey shoulder panel.
- **R005**: Black sleeve — likely the black leather sleeve.
- **R006**: White sleeve — likely the white denim sleeve.
- **R007**: Black panel — likely the black leather front panel.

→ All these regions (R003, R004, R005, R006, R007) are parts of the **same jacket** — a patchwork denim/leather jacket with white and black panels.

#### VIEW 36601262_02:
- **R008**: Close-up of the collar and upper chest — white and black panels, silver buttons, grey shoulder panel.

→ This is the **same jacket** as in previous views — consistent fabric, color, and construction.

#### VIEW 36601262_03:
- **R009**: Front view of the jacket — same as above, white and black panels, silver buttons.
- **R010**: Black pants — this is a **separate garment** (trousers), not part of the jacket.

→ R009 is the same jacket. R010 is a different garment.

#### VIEW 36601262_04:
- **R011**: Back view of the jacket — white back, grey shoulder panel, black sleeve panels.
- **R012**: Black pants — same as R010.
- **R013**: Black sleeve — same as R005.
- **R014**: Black panel — same as R007.

→ R011, R013, R014 are parts of the **same jacket**.

---

### Garment Tracking:

We now check which garment is visible in **every view**.

#### The Jacket:
- **VIEW 00**: R001 (front right side)
- **VIEW 01**: R003, R004, R005, R006, R007 (all parts of jacket)
- **VIEW 02**: R008 (collar/upper chest)
- **VIEW 03**: R009 (front view)
- **VIEW 04**: R011, R013, R014 (back and sleeves)

✅ The jacket is visible in **every view** via at least one region.

#### The Pants:
- **VIEW 03**: R010
- **VIEW 04**: R012

❌ Not present in VIEW 00, 01, or 02 → **Not in every view**.

#### The Label (R002):
- Only in VIEW 00 → Not in every view.

#### Other regions:
- R003, R005, R007, R013, R014 — all parts of the same jacket.
- R004, R006, R008, R009, R011 — also parts of the same jacket.

---

### Conclusion:

Only **one garment** — the **white and black patchwork denim/leather jacket** — is visible in **every view** via at least one mask region.

All regions that belong to this jacket are:

- R001 (VIEW 00)
- R003, R004, R005, R006, R007 (VIEW 01)
- R008 (VIEW 02)
- R009 (VIEW 03)
- R011, R013, R014 (VIEW 04)

Note: R002, R010, R012 are not part of this garment and are excluded.

---

### Final Output:

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "garment": "White and black patchwork denim/leather jacket with silver buttons, grey shoulder panel, and mixed fabric construction",
      "regions": [
        "R001",
        "R003",
        "R004",
        "R005",
        "R006",
        "R007",
        "R008",
        "R009",
        "R011",
        "R013",
        "R014"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The key is to track the same garment across all views by matching fabric, construction, color, and context — even if shown from different angles, partially, or in close-up.

---

### Step-by-step Analysis:

We have 5 views: 00, 01, 02, 03, 04.

Each view has a set of mask regions (R IDs) that are available.

We must find garments that appear in **at least one region in every view**.

---

#### View 04 (Back view):
Regions: R001, R002, R003, R004  
- R001: Black fabric, likely sleeve or shoulder panel  
- R002: Black sleeve cuff  
- R003: Black trousers  
- R004: White jacket back (main body)

#### View 03 (Front view):
Regions: R005, R006  
- R005: Black trousers (same as R003)  
- R006: Front of white/black jacket (same as R004)

#### View 02 (Close-up collar):
Regions: R007  
- R007: Collar and upper front of jacket (same as R006/R004)

#### View 01 (Side view):
Regions: R008, R009, R010, R011, R012  
- R008: Black front panel of jacket  
- R009: White sleeve  
- R010: Black sleeve cuff  
- R011: Side of jacket (white and black panels)  
- R012: Black trousers (same as R003/R005)

#### View 00 (Close-up pocket):
Regions: R013, R014  
- R013: Label patch (black and white photo)  
- R014: White jacket front with pocket and buttons (same as R006/R007)

---

### Garment Tracking:

We now look for garments that appear in **every view**.

---

#### Garment 1: The White/Black Patchwork Jacket

This is the central garment. It appears in:

- View 04: R004 (back)
- View 03: R006 (front)
- View 02: R007 (collar/upper front)
- View 01: R008 (black front panel), R009 (white sleeve), R010 (black cuff), R011 (side)
- View 00: R014 (front pocket area)

→ **All views covered.**

This is one garment, even though it appears in multiple regions per view. The regions are parts of the same jacket: white and black panels, sleeves, collar, buttons, pockets.

---

#### Garment 2: Black Trousers

Appears in:

- View 04: R003
- View 03: R005
- View 01: R012

→ **Missing in View 02 and View 00.**

Therefore, **not present in every view** → **excluded.**

---

Only appears in View 00 → **not in every view** → **excluded.**

---

#### Other regions:

- R001 (black shoulder/sleeve) — appears in View 04 only
- R002 (black cuff) — View 04 only
- R007 — View 02 only
- R008, R009, R010, R011 — View 01 only

None of these appear in all views.

---

### Conclusion:

Only **one garment** is visible in **every view**: the **white and black patchwork jacket**, represented by regions:

- R004 (View 04)
- R006 (View 03)
- R007 (View 02)
- R008, R009, R010, R011 (View 01)
- R014 (View 00)

Note: R008, R009, R010, R011 are all parts of the same jacket — they are not separate garments.

  ]

Do not join different clothes merely because they touch or share a color. Actual background pixels, mixed unrelated masks, and genuinely unidentifiable contents must not be joined.

C: uncertain or mixed
